input.message:
Real, but only for existing changelogs whose first line isn't this package's title.

Cause: `prepend` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/write.rs` (lines ~61-76). It strips a leading H1 only if it is `# {display_name}` or an ecosystem alias (`strip_alias_title`: cargo/npm/pypi prefix). Otherwise the `else` branch emits a fresh `# {display_name}` and keeps the whole old file as the body. The one existing test (`prepend_else_branch_inserts_h1_header...`) only checks the new H1 comes first, not that the old one is gone.

I ran `callisto_graph::changelog::prepend` through a throwaway crate in /tmp/claude-501/probe, with display_name `my-pkg` and rendered `## 2.0.0

- New
`. The repo is unmodified.

Observed outputs:
- Input `# Changelog

## 1.0.0

- Old
` gives `# my-pkg

## 2.0.0

- New

# Changelog

## 1.0.0...`. Two H1s.
- `# other-name` gives the same duplicate.
- `<!-- keep -->
# my-pkg

## 1.0.0...` gives a new `# my-pkg` on top, then `<!-- keep -->
# my-pkg` again. Two H1s.
- `---
title: x
---
